successors.name: British Gold Coast
successors.text: the kingdom at Akwamufie, 'independent kingdom' to 1886 in the infobox

ledger.x: c. 1629: the Akwamu state is first on record. 'The Akwamu Empire was an Akan state that rose in the 17th century'; 'The earliest reference to Akwamu appears on a Dutch Map of the Gold Coast dated to 1629'; the infobox gives '16th century' for the start. The founding year is not on the page; 1629 is the first dated…
1677: Ansa Sasraku I attacks the Ga of Accra.
1681: the Ga war ends in Akwamu's victory; Accra a province for fifty years.
1702 (May): Whydah falls to Akwamu and pays tribute.
1730: the Akyem coalition destroys Nyanaoase and takes the western lands.
1886: the independent Akwamu kingdom ends (infobox '1886 (as independent kingdom)').

wars.name: Akwamu-Ga war
wars.outcome: Akwamu victory: Ladoku overrun in 1679, the remaining Ga towns defeated 1680-81; Accra a province of Akwamu for fifty years.

wars.name: Akwamu campaign against Agona
wars.outcome: 'In 1689, Ansa Sasraku led his final major military campaign against the kingdom of Agona'; the page gives no result or land.

wars.name: Akwamu seizure of Christiansborg
wars.outcome: Akwamu forces seized Christiansborg Castle from the Danes in 1693; the page gives no end (the Danish dossier has the Danes back in 1694).

wars.name: Akwamu conquest of Little Popo and Whydah
wars.outcome: A first invasion across the Volta was repelled in early 1702; Little Popo was captured in April and Whydah seized in May; Whydah stayed tributary for over two decades.

wars.name: Akyem invasion of Akwamu
wars.outcome: Akyem and allies destroyed Nyanaoase in 1730 and Akwamu lost its western territories in the 1730-31 invasion; a smaller state formed at Akwamufie in the early 1730s.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier; the shapes are circles and regions standing for named towns and peoples.
